newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador sees main oil duct repaired ahead of time.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador sees main oil duct repaired ahead of time.

text.p: Ecuador said Friday that repair work on its main oil pipeline, the TransEcuadorean duct, was making good progress and could be finished ahead of schedule.

"Our people are working adequately. We were expecting the engines to be ready in 20 days, but now it seems they could be ready sooner," Rafael Almeida, head of the state-run oil firm Petroecuador told a TV interviewer.
A pump engine in the pipeline broke earlier this month when one of its gears snapped due to a lack of maintenance.
The mishap has reduced oil flows in the pipeline by around 30,000 barrels a day. Ecuador produces some 390,000 barrels of crude per day, of which 330,000 are carried by the TransEcuadorean duct.
Ecuador is Latin America's third largest oil exporter, behind Mexico and Venezuela. Oil revenues help finance nearly half the country's budget.
